definition: Incongruent means out of keeping — the formal word for things, such as tones or claims, that fail to fit each other.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word incongruent. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know incongruent should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: A lullaby drifted over the mall's fire alarm, an incongruent pairing nobody at the help desk could explain.
Odd just means a little unexpected — it stops short of incongruent, where two things actively fail to fit together.
Contradictory goes further than incongruent: incongruent things sit badly together, while contradictory ones cannot both be true.

Mismatched is the everyday word for concrete pairs put together wrongly — socks, gloves, chairs. Incongruent does the same job in formal writing, and for bigger mismatches: a tone against a setting, a claim against the evidence. If you can hold both objects in your hands, mismatched is the honest choice.

Clashing things fight each other loudly and visibly — colors, patterns, personalities at war. Incongruent is quieter and more formal: the pieces merely fail to fit, without any active battle. A plaid tie on a striped shirt clashes; a jokey caption under a solemn photograph is incongruent.

Inconsistent means failing to agree from one statement or action to the next — a witness whose story keeps changing. Incongruent compares two things side by side at the same moment: a tone out of keeping with its setting. Inconsistency unfolds over time; incongruence sits in a single pairing.
